observer: Hermes GPT-6.1 Sol high (offline tree audit)

findings.summary: Required clickable actions have non-empty tree labels
findings.expected: Each clickable required action has text or content-desc

observed.iconOnlyNamedAction: Navigate up ImageButton is labeled; star has descriptive text

limits: Non-empty labels do not prove spoken wording or understandable context for generic swipe labels.

findings.summary: Swipe Favorite/Remove actions lack an exposed button role
findings.expected: Button actions expose Button/ImageButton class or checkable semantics
limits: Clickable=true provides an action flag but is not an exposed button role. No speech was captured.

findings.summary: All and Favorites expose opposite selected states
Track checkbox flags agree with exposed checked/unchecked glyphs
findings.expected: Named CheckBox; checkable=true; checked matches child ☑/☐
limits: Visible state here means glyph text in XML, not pixel inspection.

findings.summary: Breakfast star exposes label and selected changes on/off
findings.expected: Favorite toggle state changes via label or checked/selected
limits: This proves tree-state changes in the captured C06 sequence, not announcements.

findings.summary: Ionic detail states are available, but not an actual before/after star-toggle sequence
findings.expected: University of Ionic (4) before and after star activation

observed.cause: F03b list swipe Favorite action; not a detail star toggle
observed.coverage: Requested exact Ionic star-action pair unavailable in this input run; do not substitute Breakfast or cross-run data as that pair

limits: Different captures/processes; no causal Ionic star-toggle claim. C06 actual star sequence is Breakfast (1).

findings.summary: Complete row subtrees contain title/time/room/track; clipped bottom rows omit context
findings.expected: Title plus time/room/track is present on a row or its children

observed.parentDescription: Row clickable content-desc is title only; metadata is nonfocusable child text

limits: Partial Ionic Tooling at the viewport bottom is not evidence of permanently missing data. Accessibility reachability/grouping needs manual traversal.

findings.summary: Parent labels repeat as child text, without a second explicit focusable node
findings.expected: Avoid duplicate stops for one control

observed.interpretation: Repeated labels in tree are not by themselves duplicate TalkBack focus stops; child text is focusable=false/clickable=false

limits: No TalkBack traversal or focus order; cannot exclude auto-focusable text or announcement duplication. Multiple generic Favorite nodes are separate controls, not same-control child duplicates.

findings.summary: Closed swipe panels remain clickable and focusable in the dumped tree
findings.expected: Closed/hidden action panels must not expose actionable/focusable buttons

observed.comparison: F01-all row1 content x76..1004 covers panel x786..1038; F01-add-reveal content x42..752 uncovers row1 panel, whose flags stay true; other rows remain closed

limits: FAIL is tree exposure, not proof TalkBack announces or activates an obscured action. Closed/revealed assignment comes from indexed F01 captures plus sibling geometry.

findings.summary: Filter close/apply/bulk actions are labeled buttons; top and final track fit
findings.expected: Named close, Reset, Deselect All, Select All, Done and bottom track

observed.note: Top and bottom are both present in each selected default-font filter XML; no distinct bottom-scroll is required/claimed. Done is at the top, not below tracks.

limits: No focus containment/return or functional activation credit. E06-bottom refers to schedule pre-scroll, not filter scrolling.

findings.summary: Alert buttons have text labels and clickable=true
findings.expected: OK / CANCEL / REMOVE are named and clickable
limits: No dialog focus containment or return tested.

findings.summary: Dark alert retains its named OK Button
findings.expected: Dark captured alert exposes the same labeled action
limits: No pixel, contrast or spoken-announcement conclusion.

findings.summary: Speech, traversal and container focus behavior are outside offline tree evidence
findings.expected: Usable order and state announcements without duplicate traps

observed.interpretation: List/scroll/button-panel containers are not unlabeled required clickable actions; their TalkBack stops remain unverified

limits: D10: no device, no speech, no traversal. XML preorder is not claimed as accessibility focus order.

findings.summary: Row entry is clickable with title but uses generic View class
findings.expected: Understandable entry role as well as label

observed.interpretation: Title and click action exist, but an explicit button/link semantic class is absent; spoken role unknown

limits: Not conflated with labeled Button controls or native checkbox roles.
